🐛 Describe the bug
When a torch.compiled function takes a Python int argument, computes a derived expression from it (e.g. + 1), and a mask_mod closure captures that derived sym-int and is used in flex_attention(...), Inductor crashes on the second call with a different int value with:
InductorError: LoweringException: AttributeError:
    'ShapeAsConstantBuffer' object has no attribute 'dtype'
  target: flex_attention

This appears to be a sibling of #157833 (closed 2025-07-11 as fixed). The simple-int-closure case from #157833 does work on the latest nightly, but a derived sym-int closure — a more general pattern that arises naturally e.g. in ring-buffer KV-cache decode — still hits the same ShapeAsConstantBuffer.get_dtype() failure.
Repro
import torch
from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import flex_attention, create_block_mask

def fn(q, k, v, current_pos: int):
    P_plus = current_pos + 1                  # derived sym-int OUTSIDE the closure
    def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
        return (kv_idx >= 0) & (kv_idx <= P_plus)
    bm = create_block_mask(mask_mod, B=None, H=None,
                            Q_LEN=q.shape[2], KV_LEN=k.shape[2],
                            device=q.device)
    return flex_attention(q, k, v, block_mask=bm)

B, H, M, KV_LEN, D = 1, 4, 1, 13, 64          # decode shapes; prefill also fails
q = torch.randn(B, H, M, D, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn(B, H, KV_LEN, D, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
v = torch.randn(B, H, KV_LEN, D, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)

compiled = torch.compile(fn, fullgraph=False)
compiled(q, k, v, current_pos=0)              # PASS — dynamo specializes on value
compiled(q, k, v, current_pos=5)              # FAIL — recompile with sym-int
Output:
call 1 (current_pos=0): OK
call 2 (current_pos=5): FAIL  InductorError: LoweringException:
    AttributeError: 'ShapeAsConstantBuffer' object has no attribute 'dtype'

Same failure with current_pos % 12, max(0, current_pos - 7), etc. Replacing P_plus = current_pos + 1 with current_pos directly inside the closure (i.e., raw sym-int, no arithmetic) does not trigger the bug — that's the case fixed in #157833.
Both prefill (q_seqlen > 1) and decode (q_seqlen = 1) reproduce; the failure surfaces in the parallel mask_mod_other_buffers = maybe_realize(...) calls:

torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/flex_attention.py:303 (prefill)
torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/flex_decoding.py:232 (decode)

Trigger conditions (all required)

torch.compiled function takes a Python int argument.
Function uses arithmetic on that int outside the closure to produce a derived sym-int (e.g., + 1, % R, max(0, x - W + 1)).
mask_mod closure captures the derived sym-int.
The closure is passed to create_block_mask; the BlockMask is used in flex_attention(...) inside the same compiled function.
Function is called twice with different int values. First call: dynamo value-specializes (compiles successfully). Second call: dynamo retraces with a dynamic sym-int → crash.

A closure that captures the int directly (mask_mod body contains kv_idx <= current_pos) does not crash — the bug appears specific to derived sym-int closures.
Hypothesised root cause
The derived expression (s34 + 1, PythonMod(s34, 12), Max(0, s34 - 7)) is materialized as a separate ShapeAsConstantBuffer in mask_mod_other_buffers. realize_inputs(...) calls ExternKernel.copy_input(x) which invokes x.get_dtype(). ShapeAsConstantBuffer has no dtype attribute → AttributeError. The path works fine for tensor mask_mod_other_buffers (real TensorBox / StorageBox).
A direct sym-int (raw closure capture of current_pos) is propagated as a graph input that already exists in the FX graph signature — so it doesn't end up as a new mask_mod_other_buffers entry. The derived expression has no graph-input identity, so it's "fresh" and gets routed through the realize path.
Workaround for users
Pass the int as a [1]-shape int64 tensor instead. Dynamo treats it as a runtime input from the very first call (no value specialization → no recompile → no derived-sym-int closure). The kernel compiles once and is reused across all calls:
def fn(q, k, v, current_pos_t: torch.Tensor):
    def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
        p_plus = current_pos_t[0] + 1
        return (kv_idx >= 0) & (kv_idx <= p_plus)
    bm = create_block_mask(mask_mod, ...)
    return flex_attention(q, k, v, block_mask=bm)

compiled = torch.compile(fn)
for pos in range(5):
    compiled(q, k, v, current_pos_t=torch.tensor([pos], dtype=torch.int64, device='cuda'))
# all 5 PASS, single graph compiled
Validated: 5 consecutive calls with different current_pos_t values complete in ~3.4 s (compile) + 4 × ~0.3 ms (cached launches) on a single Triton kernel.
Related

#157833 — closed as fixed 2025-07-11; appears to have addressed the simple-int-closure case but not the derived-sym-int case.
#182275 — open, related ShapeAsConstantBuffer family bug in nested_compile_region.

Versions
PyTorch 2.13.0a0+gitdbeb1a8 (dbeb1a8)

nodes.bodyText:
Summary
When a module's forward is wrapped with torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(..., use_reentrant=False), Dynamo installs FALSE_MATCH / NONE_MATCH (and in general CONSTANT_MATCH) guards on every kwarg passed through the wrapper, regardless of whether the wrapped function actually reads them. The same call without checkpoint only guards on kwargs that are actually read. This causes recompiles when callers vary kwargs that the body never uses.
Repro
"""Compare Dynamo guard installation: direct forward vs ``checkpoint`` wrapper."""

from __future__ import annotations
import torch


class Block(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        *,
        branch: bool = False,
        unused_flag: bool = False,                  # never read
        unused_tensor: torch.Tensor | None = None,  # never read
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        y = x.sin()
        if branch:
            y = y.cos()
        return y * 2


class NoCheckpoint(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.block = Block()

    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.block(*args, **kwargs)


class WithCheckpoint(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.block = Block()

    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
            self.block, *args, use_reentrant=False, **kwargs
        )


def main() -> int:
    x = torch.randn(4, requires_grad=True)
    kwargs = dict(branch=False, unused_flag=False, unused_tensor=None)

    out_no_ac = torch.compile(backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True)(NoCheckpoint())(x, **kwargs)
    print(out_no_ac)
    print("*" * 20)
    out_with_ac = torch.compile(backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True)(WithCheckpoint())(x, **kwargs)
    print(out_with_ac)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
Run with TORCH_LOGS=+guards python repro.py.
Observed guards
NoCheckpoint ([0/0]) — only branch (which is read) gets a value guard:
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['branch'], type=<class 'bool'>
| +- FALSE_MATCH: L['kwargs']['branch'] == False
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['unused_flag'], type=<class 'bool'>
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['unused_tensor'], type=<class 'NoneType'>

WithCheckpoint ([1/0]) — every kwarg is value-specialized, including the unused ones:
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['branch'], type=<class 'bool'>
| +- FALSE_MATCH: L['kwargs']['branch'] == False
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['unused_flag'], type=<class 'bool'>
| +- FALSE_MATCH: L['kwargs']['unused_flag'] == False     # <-- unused
+- GuardManager: source=L['kwargs']['unused_tensor'], type=<class 'NoneType'>
| +- NONE_MATCH: L['kwargs']['unused_tensor'] is None     # <-- unused

Expected behavior
Kwargs that are not read inside the checkpointed body should not get value-specialization guards. At most a TYPE/structure guard (matching what the no-checkpoint path does today) should be installed, so that varying an unused kwarg's value across calls does not invalidate the cache entry.
Root cause (best guess from reading the source)
CheckpointHigherOrderVariable._call_function routes through WrapHigherOrderVariable.create_wrapped_node → speculate_subgraph. Before tracing the wrapped body, speculate_subgraph eagerly realizes every sub-arg/sub-kwarg so the resulting guards land on the parent tracer rather than the subtracer:
# torch/_dynamo/variables/higher_order_ops.py
try:
    # ensure guards on args get installed in parent subgraph
    f, sub_args, sub_kwargs = LazyVariableTracker.realize_all(
        (f, sub_args, sub_kwargs),
    )

    with tx.output.subtracer(source_target, tracer) as subtracer:
        ...
Realizing a Python-constant kwarg through VariableBuilder installs CONSTANT_MATCH, which the guard layer expands per type:
# torch/_dynamo/guards.py
def CONSTANT_MATCH(self, guard: Guard) -> None:
    val = self.get(guard.name)
    if istype(val, bool):
        self.BOOL_MATCH(guard)        # -> FALSE_MATCH / TRUE_MATCH
    elif val is None:
        self.NONE_MATCH(guard)
    elif istype(val, types.CodeType):
        self.ID_MATCH(guard)
    else:
        self.EQUALS_MATCH(guard)
The eager realize_all is correct for guard-attribution (we do not yet know which inputs the body will read, and lazy realization inside subtracer would attach guards to the wrong tracer), but it is more conservative than necessary: by the time the body has been traced we do know which kwargs went unread (their LazyVariableTrackers never realized), and for those we could install only TYPE/structure guards on the parent rather than full CONSTANT_MATCH.
In the non-checkpoint path, plain inlining keeps unread kwargs as LazyVariableTrackers, so no value guard is installed — this is the asymmetry shown above.
Impact
Activation checkpointing is typically wrapped around generic user modules where callers thread **kwargs through the wrapper. With the current behavior:

Calling the compiled module with unused_flag=True after unused_flag=False, or with unused_tensor=torch.zeros(...) after unused_tensor=None, invalidates the cache entry and triggers a recompile.
Optional kwargs with literal None defaults split the compile cache even when the body never reads them.

Both are silent / hard-to-attribute footguns: dropping the same kwargs in the wrapper before calling checkpoint(...) makes the recompile go away, but users have no signal pointing at this.
Suggested fix (sketch)
Two-pass guard installation in speculate_subgraph for HOPs that do not need eager realization for correctness:

Skip realize_all for sub_kwargs (and sub_args where applicable). Trace the body with kwargs still lazy, with lazy realization redirected to the parent tracer's guard manager (so guards still land in the parent).
After body tracing completes, inspect which LazyVariableTrackers remain unrealized. For those, install only TYPE/structure guards on the parent (or skip entirely if the existing DICT_LENGTH + TYPE_MATCH on L['kwargs'] is enough).
Realized kwargs already have correct guards.

Most invasive bit is the redirect in (1); (2)/(3) are local. The change benefits other WrapHigherOrderVariable users (cond, while_loop, scan, …) as well, though for those the conservatism is usually free since their bodies tend to consume every input.
Versions

PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu129
Python: 3.11
Backend: aot_eager, fullgraph=True
Hardware: CPU repro is enough

nodes.title: torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint causes Dynamo to install value‑specialization guards on unused kwargs, leading to spurious recompiles

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
We use FlexAttention backend in vLLM. (Thanks a lot in integrating it!) However, we observed getting different output when running the same input twice.
We wrote this script to reproduce:
import argparse
import hashlib
import math

import torch
from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import create_block_mask, flex_attention


# This is a standalone PyTorch-only repro. It mimics the relevant parts of
# vLLM PagedAttention: a physical KV cache, 16-token pages, and a
# physical_to_logical page map used inside mask_mod.

LOGICAL_LEN = 2048
SLIDING_WINDOW = 512
VLLM_PAGE_SIZE = 16
PLACEMENT_A_START = 16
PLACEMENT_B_START = 2080
NUM_QUERY_HEADS = 4
NUM_KV_HEADS = 2
HEAD_DIM = 128
SEED = 0
STALE_SCALE = 0.0
DTYPE = torch.bfloat16


def round_up(value: int, multiple: int) -> int:
    return ((value + multiple - 1) // multiple) * multiple


def sha16(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> str:
    raw = tensor.detach().contiguous().view(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy().tobytes()
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()[:16]


def summarize_tensor(name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    row = tensor[:, :, -1, :] if tensor.ndim == 4 else tensor
    row_f = row.float()
    print(
        f"{name}: shape={tuple(tensor.shape)} dtype={tensor.dtype} "
        f"tensor_sha16={sha16(tensor)} row_sha16={sha16(row)} "
        f"row_sum={row_f.sum().item():.8f} row_mean={row_f.mean().item():.8f}"
    )


def report_diff(label: str, left: torch.Tensor, right: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
    diff = (left.float() - right.float()).abs()
    num_diff = (left != right).sum().item()
    bit_eq = torch.equal(left, right)
    print(
        f"{label}: bit_eq={bit_eq} "
        f"max_abs_diff={diff.max().item():.8f} "
        f"mean_abs_diff={diff.mean().item():.8f} "
        f"num_diff={num_diff}/{left.numel()}"
    )
    print(f"  left_sha16={sha16(left)} right_sha16={sha16(right)}")
    return bit_eq


def make_mask_mod(
    physical_to_logical: torch.Tensor,
    page_size: int,
    logical_len: int,
    sliding_window: int,
):
    def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, physical_kv_idx):
        physical_page = physical_kv_idx // page_size
        physical_offset = physical_kv_idx % page_size
        logical_page = physical_to_logical[physical_page]
        logical_kv_idx = logical_page * page_size + physical_offset

        valid = (logical_page >= 0) & (logical_kv_idx < logical_len)
        causal = logical_kv_idx <= q_idx
        in_window = q_idx - logical_kv_idx < sliding_window
        return valid & causal & in_window

    return mask_mod


def make_physical_to_logical(
    start_slot: int,
    total_cache_tokens: int,
    logical_len: int,
    page_size: int,
    device: torch.device,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    if start_slot % page_size != 0:
        raise ValueError(f"start_slot={start_slot} must be page aligned")

    num_pages = total_cache_tokens // page_size
    physical_to_logical = torch.full(
        (num_pages,), -1, device=device, dtype=torch.long
    )
    start_page = start_slot // page_size
    logical_pages = round_up(logical_len, page_size) // page_size
    physical_to_logical[
        start_page : start_page + logical_pages
    ] = torch.arange(logical_pages, device=device, dtype=torch.long)
    return physical_to_logical


def make_physical_kv_cache(
    logical_key: torch.Tensor,
    logical_value: torch.Tensor,
    start_slot: int,
    total_cache_tokens: int,
    stale_scale: float,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    _, num_kv_heads, logical_len, head_dim = logical_key.shape
    device = logical_key.device
    dtype = logical_key.dtype

    if stale_scale == 0:
        key_cache = torch.zeros(
            1,
            num_kv_heads,
            total_cache_tokens,
            head_dim,
            device=device,
            dtype=dtype,
        )
        value_cache = torch.zeros(
            1,
            num_kv_heads,
            total_cache_tokens,
            head_dim,
            device=device,
            dtype=dtype,
        )
    else:
        key_cache = (
            torch.randn(
                1,
                num_kv_heads,
                total_cache_tokens,
                head_dim,
                device=device,
                dtype=torch.float32,
            )
            * stale_scale
        ).to(dtype)
        value_cache = (
            torch.randn(
                1,
                num_kv_heads,
                total_cache_tokens,
                head_dim,
                device=device,
                dtype=torch.float32,
            )
            * stale_scale
        ).to(dtype)

    key_cache[:, :, start_slot : start_slot + logical_len, :] = logical_key
    value_cache[:, :, start_slot : start_slot + logical_len, :] = logical_value
    return key_cache, value_cache


def print_block_mask_summary(label: str, block_mask) -> None:
    kv_indices = block_mask.kv_indices
    full_kv_indices = block_mask.full_kv_indices
    first_q_block_kv_count = int(block_mask.kv_num_blocks[0, 0, 0].item())
    first_q_block_kv = (
        kv_indices[0, 0, 0, : min(first_q_block_kv_count, 16)]
        .detach()
        .cpu()
        .tolist()
    )
    print(
        f"{label}: BLOCK_SIZE={block_mask.BLOCK_SIZE} "
        f"shape={block_mask.shape} "
        f"kv_indices_shape={tuple(kv_indices.shape)} "
        f"kv_num_blocks_sum={int(block_mask.kv_num_blocks.sum().item())}"
    )
    print(
        f"{label}: q_block0 kv_num_blocks={first_q_block_kv_count} "
        f"kv_indices[:16]={first_q_block_kv}"
    )
    if full_kv_indices is not None and block_mask.full_kv_num_blocks is not None:
        first_q_block_full_count = int(block_mask.full_kv_num_blocks[0, 0, 0].item())
        first_q_block_full = (
            full_kv_indices[0, 0, 0, : min(first_q_block_full_count, 16)]
            .detach()
            .cpu()
            .tolist()
        )
        print(
            f"{label}: full_kv_num_blocks_sum="
            f"{int(block_mask.full_kv_num_blocks.sum().item())} "
            f"q_block0 full_kv_num_blocks={first_q_block_full_count} "
            f"full_kv_indices[:16]={first_q_block_full}"
        )


def run_case(
    label: str,
    query: torch.Tensor,
    key_cache: torch.Tensor,
    value_cache: torch.Tensor,
    physical_to_logical: torch.Tensor,
    args,
    compiled_flex,
    block_size: tuple[int, int],
    kernel_options: dict[str, int | bool],
) -> torch.Tensor:
    mask_mod = make_mask_mod(
        physical_to_logical=physical_to_logical,
        page_size=args.page_size,
        logical_len=args.logical_len,
        sliding_window=args.sliding_window,
    )
    block_mask = create_block_mask(
        mask_mod,
        None,
        None,
        args.logical_len,
        args.total_cache_tokens,
        device=query.device,
        BLOCK_SIZE=block_size,
    )
    print_block_mask_summary(label, block_mask)

    out = compiled_flex(
        query,
        key_cache,
        value_cache,
        None,
        block_mask,
        scale=args.scale,
        enable_gqa=args.num_query_heads != args.num_kv_heads,
        kernel_options=kernel_options,
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    summarize_tensor(f"{label}: out", out)
    return out


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=(
            "Pure PyTorch repro for physical-placement-dependent "
            "FlexAttention outputs with a vLLM-style 16-token paged KV cache. "
            "Pass only the FlexAttention BlockMask token size to test: 128 or 16."
        )
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "flex_block_size",
        type=int,
        choices=(16, 128),
        help=(
            "FlexAttention BlockMask token block size. Use 128 to reproduce "
            "placement-dependent output; use 16 to align with the vLLM page "
            "size and remove the difference in this repro."
        ),
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def run() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("This repro requires CUDA.")
    if NUM_QUERY_HEADS % NUM_KV_HEADS != 0:
        raise ValueError("num_query_heads must be a multiple of num_kv_heads")

    device = torch.device("cuda")
    args.logical_len = LOGICAL_LEN
    args.sliding_window = SLIDING_WINDOW
    args.page_size = VLLM_PAGE_SIZE
    args.start_a = PLACEMENT_A_START
    args.start_b = PLACEMENT_B_START
    args.num_query_heads = NUM_QUERY_HEADS
    args.num_kv_heads = NUM_KV_HEADS
    args.head_dim = HEAD_DIM
    args.scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(HEAD_DIM)
    min_total = max(PLACEMENT_A_START, PLACEMENT_B_START) + LOGICAL_LEN
    args.total_cache_tokens = round_up(min_total, max(128, VLLM_PAGE_SIZE))

    print(f"torch={torch.__version__} cuda={torch.version.cuda}")
    print(
        f"device={torch.cuda.get_device_name()} "
        f"capability={torch.cuda.get_device_capability()}"
    )
    print(
        f"logical_len={LOGICAL_LEN} sliding_window={SLIDING_WINDOW} "
        f"vllm_page_size={VLLM_PAGE_SIZE} "
        f"flex_block_size={args.flex_block_size} "
        f"total_cache_tokens={args.total_cache_tokens}"
    )
    print(
        f"placement_a start={PLACEMENT_A_START} "
        f"start%128={PLACEMENT_A_START % 128}; "
        f"placement_b start={PLACEMENT_B_START} "
        f"start%128={PLACEMENT_B_START % 128}"
    )
    print(f"inactive physical KV scale={STALE_SCALE}")

    torch.manual_seed(SEED)
    query = torch.randn(
        1,
        NUM_QUERY_HEADS,
        LOGICAL_LEN,
        HEAD_DIM,
        device=device,
        dtype=torch.float32,
    ).to(DTYPE)
    logical_key = torch.randn(
        1,
        NUM_KV_HEADS,
        LOGICAL_LEN,
        HEAD_DIM,
        device=device,
        dtype=torch.float32,
    ).to(DTYPE)
    logical_value = torch.randn(
        1,
        NUM_KV_HEADS,
        LOGICAL_LEN,
        HEAD_DIM,
        device=device,
        dtype=torch.float32,
    ).to(DTYPE)

    key_a, value_a = make_physical_kv_cache(
        logical_key,
        logical_value,
        PLACEMENT_A_START,
        args.total_cache_tokens,
        STALE_SCALE,
    )
    key_b, value_b = make_physical_kv_cache(
        logical_key,
        logical_value,
        PLACEMENT_B_START,
        args.total_cache_tokens,
        STALE_SCALE,
    )
    p2l_a = make_physical_to_logical(
        PLACEMENT_A_START,
        args.total_cache_tokens,
        LOGICAL_LEN,
        VLLM_PAGE_SIZE,
        device,
    )
    p2l_b = make_physical_to_logical(
        PLACEMENT_B_START,
        args.total_cache_tokens,
        LOGICAL_LEN,
        VLLM_PAGE_SIZE,
        device,
    )

    active_a = key_a[:, :, PLACEMENT_A_START : PLACEMENT_A_START + LOGICAL_LEN, :]
    active_b = key_b[:, :, PLACEMENT_B_START : PLACEMENT_B_START + LOGICAL_LEN, :]
    report_diff("active logical key placement_b vs placement_a", active_b, active_a)
    active_value_a = value_a[
        :, :, PLACEMENT_A_START : PLACEMENT_A_START + LOGICAL_LEN, :
    ]
    active_value_b = value_b[
        :, :, PLACEMENT_B_START : PLACEMENT_B_START + LOGICAL_LEN, :
    ]
    report_diff(
        "active logical value placement_b vs placement_a",
        active_value_b,
        active_value_a,
    )

    compiled_flex = torch.compile(flex_attention, fullgraph=True, mode="default")
    flex_block_size = args.flex_block_size
    block_size = (flex_block_size, flex_block_size)
    kernel_options: dict[str, int | bool] = {"FORCE_USE_FLEX_ATTENTION": False}
    if flex_block_size == VLLM_PAGE_SIZE:
        kernel_options["BLOCK_M"] = flex_block_size
        kernel_options["BLOCK_N"] = flex_block_size

    print(f"\n=== FlexAttention BlockMask: BLOCK_SIZE={block_size} ===")
    out_a = run_case(
        f"placement_a_block{flex_block_size}",
        query,
        key_a,
        value_a,
        p2l_a,
        args,
        compiled_flex,
        block_size=block_size,
        kernel_options=kernel_options,
    )
    out_b = run_case(
        f"placement_b_block{flex_block_size}",
        query,
        key_b,
        value_b,
        p2l_b,
        args,
        compiled_flex,
        block_size=block_size,
        kernel_options=kernel_options,
    )
    report_diff(
        f"block{flex_block_size} placement_b vs placement_a",
        out_b,
        out_a,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()
This is a standalone PyTorch-only repro for a paged-KV/FlexAttention
interaction. It does not depend on vLLM or any local model architecture.
The script simulates:

a vLLM-like physical KV cache;
16-token KV pages;
a physical_to_logical page map used inside mask_mod;
two placements of the same logical K/V sequence at different physical cache
offsets;
FlexAttention with BlockMask.BLOCK_SIZE=(128, 128) vs (16, 16).

The two placements contain bit-identical active logical K/V data and represent
the same logical causal sliding-window attention problem. With 128-token
FlexAttention sparse blocks, the outputs differ. With 16-token sparse blocks
aligned to the page size, the outputs are bit-identical.
Inactive physical KV slots are zeros by default, so the repro does not rely on
reading stale data from other requests.

dtype=bfloat16

The simulated vLLM page size is fixed to 16 tokens.

Why this matters for vLLM-style inference
vLLM's paged KV cache commonly uses 16-token pages. If FlexAttention builds a
BlockMask with the default 128-token block size, each FlexAttention KV block
spans 8 vLLM pages.
For the same logical request, different physical cache placements can start at
different offsets inside a 128-token FlexAttention block. Example:
placement A starts at physical slot 16   -> offset 16 within a 128-token block
placement B starts at physical slot 2080 -> offset 32 within a 128-token block

The same logical sliding-window attention is then decomposed into different
FlexAttention sparse block schedules. In bf16, this changes the block-wise
online softmax/reduction order and produces different outputs. In greedy
inference, these small output differences can propagate to raw logits and
eventually change generated text at temperature=0.
Question
Is this physical-placement-dependent output expected for equivalent
FlexAttention masks with different sparse block schedules?
If this is expected numerically, the actionable requirement for vLLM-style
paged inference seems to be: the FlexAttention BlockMask.BLOCK_SIZE should
match the paged KV cache size when mask_mod maps physical KV indices back to
logical indices at page granularity.

Summary
Under torch 2.12.0+cu130 + triton 3.7.0 on B200, vLLM's MoE Refactor Integration Test (B200 - TEMPORARY) fails its GSM8K accuracy check on the Nemotron-Nano-30B-Fp8-ModelOpt model when served with the flashinfer-trtllm backend. The engine compiles and runs to completion, but the model produces ~21% correct GSM8K answers vs an expected floor of 0.21 (= 0.29 - 0.08 tolerance).
FAILED evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py::test_gsm8k_correctness[Nemotron-Nano-30B-Fp8-ModelOpt-fi-trtllm]
AssertionError: GSM8K metric too low: 0.2085 < 0.2900 - 0.0800 = 0.2100
assert np.float64(0.20849128127369218) >= (0.29 - 0.08)

This is a numerical / accuracy regression — not a fake-kernel / stride bug. No Engine core init failed, no Server exited unexpectedly, no moe_forward stride assertion in the log.
Environment

torch: 2.12.0+cu130 (test channel)
triton: 3.7.0
CUDA: 13.0 / Driver: 570.x
Python: 3.12
Hardware: NVIDIA B200
vLLM: release_212_tests branch, commit 54590d5162
Model: Nemotron-Nano-30B-Fp8-ModelOpt (FP8 ModelOpt quantization)
Backend: flashinfer + trtllm path (fi-trtllm)

Reproducibility on torch 2.12 branch

Passes on every recent main build (torch 2.11):

64094 (2026-05-02 daily): passed
64227 (2026-05-03 daily): passed
64258 (2026-05-03 nightly): passed

The regression appeared between 64097 (passing) and 64468 (failing), within the test-PR rebase from main. Strongest suspects — commits in this delta that touch flashinfer / fp8 / trtllm / Nemotron:

c51df4300 Disable flashinfer autotune temporarily due to correctness issues (#41524)
c3868bbbe Add FlashInfer FP8 async TP fusion and preserve allreduce fusion ordering (#39505)
a3c83ff2f Faster per-token fp8 group quant packed kernel for blackwell (#41326)
db9a84e0c [Bugfix] Fix FP8 Bias Loading (#41424)
8c780943b Fix Nano Nemotron text-only weight loading (#41205)
8decbfa02 Test nemotron nano-v2 and nemotron nano-v3 separately, disable super-omni redundant tests (#41616)

Reproduction
tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py::test_gsm8k_correctness[Nemotron-Nano-30B-Fp8-ModelOpt-fi-trtllm]

Driven via:
.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-moe-refactor-integration-test.sh

or manually via the GSM8K eval harness with the Nemotron-Nano-30B-Fp8-ModelOpt-fi-trtllm config.
Diagnosis request
The accuracy regression is borderline (0.2085 vs 0.2100, just 0.0015 below the floor) but reproducibly below threshold on torch 2.12 while torch 2.11 main builds clear it consistently. Likely candidates: numerical drift in the flashinfer FP8 + trtllm Blackwell path, or a fusion / scheduling change in Inductor that subtly alters fp8 dequantization order.
This fits the same family as previously filed accuracy-drift issues on the torch 2.12 branch (now closed): #181169 (gsm8k 0.54 -> 0.48), #181249 (PRM-7B logits), #181633 (Elastic EP 0.000), #181634 (CPU offload w4a16). The pattern: triton 3.7 / Inductor 2.12 changes producing measurable numerical drift in FP8 / quantized kernel paths.
Could pytorch confirm whether triton 3.7 introduced any numerical-precision changes to the flashinfer FP8 kernels (or fp8 dequant epilogues) on Blackwell?

🐛 Describe the bug
index_add (possibly index_reduce also) had a 3-4x perf degradation on AMD gpus.

import time

# Test different index patterns

for ind_range in ind_ranges:
    ind = torch.randint(0, ind_range, size=(src_size,), device='cuda')

    # Warmup
    for _ in range(10):
        x.index_add_(0, ind, src)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    # Benchmark
    start_time = time.time()
    for i in range(50):
        x.index_add_(0, ind, src)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    end_time = time.time()
    mean_time = (end_time - start_time)/50

linux-jammy-py3.9-gcc11 / test (docs_test, 1, 1, lf.linux.2xlarge)

Compare the preview of the pages you converted with the same pages on the main branch.
